l1_words.meaning: to intend or plan to do something
to watch or to be present at an event
having a cold (an illness with a runny nose)
possibly, or from time to time

pattern_explanation: Each of these Portuguese words looks like an English word because both languages borrowed it from Latin or developed it from the same root. Over time the meanings drifted apart, so the shared form now points to a different meaning in English.
false_friend_warning: The Portuguese word written as 'pretender' looks like the English verb 'pretend', but it means 'intend' or 'plan'. A Portuguese speaker may wrongly say 'he pretends to come' when they mean 'he intends to come'.
